_comment: Real AUTO-role-detection prototype config for the final ESP32-H2 SuperMini graduation-project hardware (see docs/pogo-interface.md 'confirmed GPIO profile' and README's wiring section). This board's permanently-paired sensor is a ROHM BH1750 (ambient light / illuminance). dev_mode=AUTO: ROOT/INTERMEDIATE/LEAF is derived at runtime from real BASE_ID + DETECT_IN/OUT + PEER_HELLO, never forced. Both prototype configs (this file and prototype_sht45.json) share the EXACT SAME upstream_port/downstream_port block -- the only per-board differences are driver_id, i2c_address, sensor_type_bitmap and calibration, exactly as section 2 of the follow-up spec requires.
_driver_comment: SENSOR_DRIVER_ID_BH1750 and the ILLUMINANCE channel bit are resolved by name -- see prototype_sht45.json's _driver_comment for how tools/pack_module_config.py keeps this in sync with the C headers.
_addr_comment: BH1750 ADDR pin LOW or floating -> 7-bit address 0x23 (most breakout boards pull ADDR low/leave it floating by default -- CONFIRM the actual breakout's ADDR strap before flashing; if it is tied HIGH instead, the address is 0x5C and this field must change to match, per section 4 of the follow-up spec: 'ADDR 상태에 맞는 주소').
_calibration_comment: calibration[0] is an optional lux correction-factor override in milli-units (0 = use the driver's default MTreg/1.2 conversion, no correction) -- see components/bh1750/bh1750.c.
_timeout_comment: BH1750 one-time high-resolution mode takes up to 180ms per the datasheet; 300ms leaves margin for I2C bus contention/retries.
_upstream_comment: Identical to prototype_sht45.json's upstream_port -- see that file's _upstream_comment for why DETECT_IN is GPIO12/DETECT_OUT is GPIO2 (deep-sleep-ready profile, swapped from the earlier DETECT_IN=2/DETECT_OUT=12), and for the required rewiring before flashing.
_downstream_comment: Identical to prototype_sht45.json's downstream_port (including its DETECT_OUT=GPIO3 move from GPIO22, this follow-up, config_revision bumped 1->2 -- see that file's _downstream_comment and docs/pogo-interface.md's GPIO history section).
